Formulation
- Brief summary:
  - Predisposing factors: No significant past medical or psychiatric history recorded.
  - Precipitating factors: Recent exposure to brother with similar symptoms; probable infectious gastroenteritis onset 3 days prior.
  - Perpetuating factors: Persistent vomiting preventing retention of ORS/fluids, ongoing diarrhoea and abdominal cramping centered around umbilicus, not improving after 2–3 days.
  - Protective factors: Lives with family who can provide support; patient willing to attend urgent clinic for assessment and stool testing; able to pass urine (suggesting some hydration remained).

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Acute diarrhoea with vomiting and fever — suspected infectious gastroenteritis; risk of dehydration.
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Symptom improvement/resolution; remain adequately hydrated; avoid escalation to emergency care if possible.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Assess hydration status; obtain stool sample for microbiology; identify if bacterial cause requiring targeted treatment; provide safety advice and escalate to A&E if clinical deterioration.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue ORS in very small, frequent sips (as advised).
  - Attend urgent clinic appointment for assessment and stool sample submission (appointment to be booked via support line).
  - Monitor urine output and general condition; seek immediate care (A&E) if feeling significantly worse or unable to maintain any fluids.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Book an urgent in-person clinic appointment for hydration assessment and to collect/post stool sample.
  - Assess for dehydration at clinic (clinical assessment), and arrange appropriate investigations/treatment based on results.
  - Consider specific antimicrobial therapy if stool testing indicates a bacterial pathogen per local guidelines.
  - Provide clear A&E escalation criteria and reinforce small frequent sips of ORS; advise simple bland foods if tolerated and avoidance of milk/fruit/vegetables that may worsen symptoms (as discussed).

Secondary Problem:
- Abdominal pain localized to periumbilical/around navel; cramping associated with bowel motions and urgency.
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Pain relief and improved abdominal comfort.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Assess severity and cause of abdominal pain; exclude complications (e.g., severe abdominal pathology) during clinic assessment.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Report pain severity and any new features (increasing intensity, spreading, fever worsening, blood in stool) at clinic or urgently if worsens.
  - Use previously tolerated PRN measures (e.g., ibuprofen for menstrual cramps) only as previously used and report usage at clinic (ibuprofen use documented; dose not recorded).
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Examine abdomen at urgent appointment; assess for focal signs or requirement for imaging or emergency referral.
  - Manage pain appropriately based on findings and consider further investigations if clinically indicated.

Tertiary Problem:
- Not recorded.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Use of oral rehydration salts in very small, frequent sips.
  - Dietary advice: simple bland foods if tolerated (toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, milk while symptomatic.
  - Rationale for stool sample testing to identify bacterial causes and guide treatment.
  - Advice to attend A&E if symptoms worsen or if unable to maintain hydration.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Worsening overall condition or "feeling more unwell" (clinician advised escalation to A&E if more unwell).
  - Continued inability to retain any fluids despite small sips.
  - Not recorded: No other specific early warning signs documented.
- Coping Strategies:
  - Small, frequent sips of ORS; rest at home; work from home until symptoms improve; engage family support.
